Definition: from G1722 and a derivative of G2524; subinduced, i.e. surreptitiously suborned as a lier-in-wait:--spy.
BiblicalUsage: The chief priests sent spies in Luke 20:20 — men feigning themselves just, watching Jesus to take hold of His words and deliver Him to the governor.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the spies' question about Caesar was a trap, and Jesus turned the trap into teaching — render to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
